text: Short-circuit source_has_ingestible_content in src/workspace/serve_discovery.rs (line ~333). It currently eagerly walks the entire source tree via WalkDir, collects every format-matching relative path, then calls graphtor_core::acquire::filter_files once and checks non-empty. The caller (serve auto-discovery ServeMode classification) only needs a boolean, so serve startup pays a full traversal and retains memory proportional to document count, and background sync scans the same tree again. Optimization: compile the format matcher and include/exclude glob matcher once, then return true as soon as the first file passes BOTH the format check AND the include/exclude filter. Care needed: filter_files is currently a batch API, so a correct short-circuit must apply the glob include/exclude semantics per file (empty include = include all, exclude wins) without changing which files count as ingestible. Add a regression test asserting an excluded-only tree returns false and that a large tree returns true after inspecting only the first eligible file. Source: PR 90 wave-7 Copilot performance finding on serve_discovery.rs:342. Deferred from 045-S under the review-cycle hard stop because it is genuinely new performance scope, not a correctness or containment regression.

Spike: read-only-serve cross-process coordination design. Covers deferred Copilot PR90 review items F2 (status/query read-only cross-process open hinging on the read-only-serve x-process design) and F6 (stale-lock liveness and ownership). Redesigning cross-process liveness/ownership using the filesystem-readonly-attribute as a lock is beyond the single-developer local 045-S shipment scope; investigate an ownership/liveness model before changing serve open semantics.

Served-alias handling follow-up for serve auto-discovery (deferred from Copilot PR90 review). Evaluate whether served database aliases need explicit canonicalization or reporting beyond the current dedup union.
